generated_by: hand — one entry per book whose text this project commits, written by the reading pass that committed it
_doc: THE REGISTER OF THE BOOKS THIS PROJECT HOLDS TEXT FOR. It exists for the same reason data/research/newspapers/corpus.json does: a quote is checked against a committed file, and the file has to be traceable back to the artifact it came out of or the check is circular. Each entry says what the book is, which source record grades it, where the deposit copy is and its sha256, what derived text is committed and its sha256, how that text was produced, and what has actually been read out of it. A book with no entry here has no committed text; an entry whose sha256 no longer matches means somebody edited a transcription, which is the one thing this subtree must never do. DERIVED TEXT IS COMMITTED, SCANS AND RENDERS ARE NOT: the deposit under chicago/reference/ is read-only and nothing here is published.

books.title: The Autobiography of Gurdon Saltonstall Hubbard, Pa-pa-ma-ta-be, "The Swift Walker"
books.imprint: Chicago: R. R. Donnelley & Sons Company, The Lakeside Press, Christmas 1911 — The Lakeside Classics

text.how: curl -L https://archive.org/download/autobiographyofg00hubb/autobiographyofg00hubb_djvu.txt on 2026-09-03, committed byte for byte. The identifier was confirmed against archive.org's advancedsearch API first (numFound 1, year 1911).
text.corroborated_by: pdftotext -layout over the deposited PDF's own embedded text layer, an independent extraction of the same scan, which agrees with the committed text to better than 0.9999 on whitespace-normalised comparison. The two differ only where poppler welds an italic word to its neighbour.

page_index.why: THE COMMITTED TEXT HAS NO PAGE BREAKS. The Internet Archive's djvu output carries not one form feed and prints no folio of its own, so the leaf boundaries are transferred onto it from the deposited PDF's text layer, which has all 226. 207 of the 208 non-blank leaves aligned; the one that did not is the Contents at leaf 19, whose columns poppler reorders, and it is declared as such.

books.read: Pages ix-xxvii and 27-41, 135-138, 141-144, 153-159, 165-174, 178-182, declared item by item in coverage.json. Pages 1-26, 42-134, 139-140, 145-152, 160-164, 175-177 are NOT read and are not declared: they are Montreal, Mackinaw and the Illinois River posts, and they name no Chicago.
books.note: THE SCAN IS OUT OF ORDER. Pages xv and xvi were photographed at the front of the Internet Archive item, as leaves 11 and 12, ahead of the title page. The text proves it and six folios read off the page confirm it; tools/build_book_page_index.py carries the three folio runs that forces and hard-fails if a printed folio ever contradicts them.

books.title: Fergus' Historical Series, Nos. 26-29, bound in one volume
books.imprint: Chicago: Fergus Printing Company, 1883-1888 - four separately printed pamphlets, each with its own title page and its own folio run starting at 1

text.how: The deposit's own hOCR search text, copied byte for byte on 2026-09-03. NO FETCH WAS MADE: the file had been in chicago/reference/fergus/ unread since the deposit was laid down, with its hOCR page index beside it. tools/build_book_page_index.py --build refuses to write the index unless the committed text is byte-identical to that deposit file, so the copy is gated and not merely asserted.

page_index.why: THE COMMITTED TEXT HAS NO PAGE BREAKS, AND UNLIKE HUBBARD'S IT NEEDED NO ALIGNMENT TO GET THEM. The Internet Archive emitted an hOCR PAGE INDEX with the same OCR pass that produced this text, and it gives every one of the 858 leaves an exact character range in these very characters - so the boundaries are transferred by arithmetic, not searched for, and --build hard-fails unless the 858 ranges tile the text with no gap and no overlap. They do: 624 non-blank leaves, all exact.
page_index.folio_note: 194 of 624 non-blank leaves print a folio the head-reader could take. The rest are refused rather than carried: THIS VOLUME BINDS FOUR PAMPHLETS THAT EACH RESTART AT 1, so there is no constant offset to carry and a carried folio would be an invention. The OCR loses most of the rest to its own damage - '1 843. 1 3', 'l6', 'l843- 21' - and a claim cites its LEAF, which is exact for all 858.

books.claims: chicago/4d/data/research/books/claims/fergus_26_29_first_half.json - 41 claims, 20 of them town findings, T-0499 (leaves 1-429); chicago/4d/data/research/books/claims/fergus_26_29_second_half.json - 58 claims, 45 of them town findings, T-0500 (leaves 430-858). The volume is read whole between the two.
books.read: ALL 858 LEAVES, between two tickets. T-0499 read leaves 1-429 - the front matter (1-14), No. 26 entire (15-206), No. 27 entire (207-398) and No. 28 through its port statistics (399-429) - as four `list` items in coverage.json. T-0500 read leaves 430-858 as five more: No. 28's Business Directory (430-457) and Obituary (606-644) and the whole of No. 29 (658-850) read in full; the publisher's advertisement leaves (645-657, 851-858) read for Chicago titles only; and No. 28's alphabetical name directory (458-605) SWEPT BY MACHINE and NOT read continuously, which its own declaration states in as many words.
books.note: THE FILENAME SAYS 26-29 AND UNTIL THIS PASS NOTHING SAID WHAT THAT MEANT. The four numbers are Harrison's Discourse on the Aborigines of the Ohio Valley (26), Beckwith's Illinois and Indiana Indians (27), the Directory of the City of Chicago for 1843 (28) and Kirby's Biographical Sketch of Joseph Duncan (29); the contents table with leaf ranges is in README.md. Two of the four touch Chicago, one of them fourteen years too early and the other eight years too late, and No. 28 - the directory 'for 1843' - was compiled in 1896. T-0500 adds what the second half holds: eight thousand 1843 directory entries whose only pre-1837 statements are Robert Fergus's own bracketed annotations, an Obituary carrying six deaths inside 1830-1836, and No. 29's canal thread - Duncan's 1829 diary of getting the route located, the legislature of 1834-35 adjourning without acting on it, and the special session of December 1835 that authorised the loan the canal was finally built with.

books.claims: chicago/4d/data/research/books/claims/ichr_v4_thompson_vincennes.json - 8 claims, all of them town findings, T-0650 (printed pages 256-259).
books.read: Pages 256-259 of Joseph J. Thompson's article 'The Illinois Part of the Diocese of Vincennes' (pages 253-265), declared in coverage.json as ONE `list` item. THE VOLUME IS COMMITTED AND FOUR PAGES OF IT ARE READ; everything else in the 290 KB is unread and undeclared, which is not a fault.
books.note: THERE IS NO DEPOSIT COPY AND NO PAGE INDEX, and both absences are on purpose. No PDF of this volume was downloaded: the reading needed four pages and the djvu OCR carries them, so a 60-plus MB scan would be a deposit nothing checks. Without a second extraction there is nothing to corroborate the OCR against, so `corroborated_by` is null and every claim taken from it is graded transcription_mediated - a reading off the page image would outrank it and none was made. The page boundaries were read off the volume's own RUNNING HEADS, which this OCR prints ('258 JOSEPH J. THOMPSON', 'ILLINOIS PART OF THE DIOCESE OF VINCENNES 259'), so no alignment was needed and tools/build_book_page_index.py is not involved; the four boundaries are written into the source record's locator instead. NOTE THE OVERLAP THAT IS NOT A DUPLICATION: data/sources/st_cyr_register_ichr_v4.json also reads this volume, through a Genealogy Trails transcription of two of its register pages rather than through this scan. Two records of one volume, exactly as chicago_antiquities_pratt and chicago_antiquities_american_fur_co are two records of one book.

books.title: H. H. Porter, A Short Autobiography, Written for His Children and Grandchildren
books.imprint: Chicago: privately printed, 1915. Written by Porter in the summer of 1904.

deposit.note: DERIVED TEXT, NOT THE SCAN. The 66 MB PDF this OCR was made from is offloaded — chicago/reference/hh-porter-a-short-autobiography.yaml names a local_archive_path outside this repository and records the scan's own sha256, cc884a721b7390aeb717753d19fa7143af8b2a09044db37e8f3a606d763030dc — so the deposit copy held here is the Internet Archive's hOCR search text for the same item, together with the hOCR page index emitted beside it (chicago/reference/hh-porter-a-short-autobiography/4582673_hocr_pageindex.json). That is the Fergus arrangement, for the Fergus reason: the index gives every leaf's exact character range in that very text.

text.how: curl -L https://archive.org/download/chicago1835-hh-porter-autobiography/4582673_hocr_searchtext.txt.gz on 2026-09-05, gunzipped, committed byte for byte. The item identifier was not searched for: chicago/reference/hh-porter-a-short-autobiography.yaml already names it, because the item is this project's own upload of its own deposit.
text.corroborated_by: The Internet Archive's djvu text of the same scan (4582673_djvu.txt), an independent serialisation of the same OCR pass, read against this one at every page the reading cites. THE DEPOSITED PDF'S OWN TEXT LAYER WAS NOT USED AND THE TICKET IS RIGHT ABOUT WHY: it uses subset encodings that come out as garbage. The djvu text was rejected as the committed text for a different reason — it carries no page breaks and no page index was emitted with it, so leaf boundaries on it would have to be aligned rather than read.

page_index.why: EXACT, NOT ALIGNED. The deposit holds the hOCR page index the Internet Archive emitted with this very text, so leaf i IS text[start:end]; --build refuses to write the file unless the seventy ranges tile the committed text end to end with no gap and no overlap, and they do. Hubbard's pdftotext transfer could not have been run here in any case: the deposit PDF is offloaded and is not in the checkout.

books.read: ALL SEVENTY LEAVES, declared as one `list` item in coverage.json. The whole volume was swept and read closely where it answered; nothing is undeclared, because the ticket's question was about the whole book and the answer had to be about the whole book.
books.note: THE BOOK CARRIES NO DOCUMENT OF CHICAGO 1830-1836 AND THAT IS ITS ENTRY HERE. Its earliest Chicago is September 1853, the author's own arrival; its author was born at Machias, Maine, on 7 December 1835, five months after the scene date; and his parents lived and died in Maine, so the family memory the ticket allowed for does not exist. Two 1853 statements are recorded as town findings — the Fort Dearborn blockhouse still standing, and the street grade five to twelve feet below 1904's — and neither is used. Text is committed for a book with eight claims on it because the verbatim gate checks quotes against a committed file, and a carries-no-document finding that cannot be re-checked is an assertion rather than a reading.

books.title: John Moses and Joseph Kirkland, History of Chicago, Illinois, volume 1
books.imprint: Chicago and New York: Munsell & Company, 1895 — one of two volumes; only volume 1 is held here

text.how: The Internet Archive's own hOCR search text for this project's own deposit item, fetched 2026-09-05 from https://archive.org/download/historyofchicago01mose_202609/historyofchicago01mose_hocr_searchtext.txt.gz, gunzipped and committed byte for byte. The hOCR page index was fetched in the same call and is deposited beside it; tools/build_book_page_index.py --build refuses to write the index unless the committed text is byte-identical to that deposit file, so the copy is gated and not merely asserted.

page_index.why: THE BOUNDARIES ARE EXACT AND NOT ALIGNED. The Internet Archive emitted the hOCR page index beside the search text, so leaf i IS text[start:end]; --build checks the 1,056 ranges tile the committed text end to end with no gap and no overlap and refuses to write otherwise. 917 leaves are non-blank and 451 print a folio in a running head this OCR could read. THE READ FOLIO IS THE OCR'S AND THE OCR MISREADS DIGITS: leaf 46 reports '94' where the page prints 24 and leaf 109 reports '88' where it prints 83. `folio_source` is 'read' throughout and never 'offset', so a wrong folio here is a wrong READING and not an invented number; every claim states the folio its author read off the running head himself.

books.read: Chapter V, leaves 99-104, and chapter VI, leaves 107-142, read closely and declared as four `list` items in coverage.json; all 1,056 leaves swept by machine for the Newberry index's forty-nine lead surnames and declared as a fifth. Everything else — the geology, 1837 to 1893, the railroad, banking, real-estate and biographical chapters, and the appendix and index — is NOT read and is not declared.
books.note: THE ITEM BUNDLES TWO DIFFERENT BOOKS AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS THIS ONE. Beside the 'mose' files the deposit carries historyofchicago01andr.pdf and .epub with their own OCR derivatives; T-0581 asked whether they were really Moses and Kirkland and they are not — historyofchicago01andr_djvu.txt opens with A. T. Andreas's own title page, 'HISTORY OF GHICACO FROM THE EARLIEST Period TO THE Present TIME. IN THREE VOLUMES. VOLUME I.— ENDING WITH THE YEAR 1857 BY A. T. ANDREAS. CHICAGO: A T. ANDREAS. PUBLISHER. 1884.' Andreas volume 1 is already held at data/sources/andreas_1884_v1.json and nothing was taken from the stray copy. Every artifact registered in this entry is from the 'mose' set. THE DEPOSIT PDF IS NOT IN THIS CHECKOUT: the 72 MB scan is offloaded and chicago/reference/moses-kirkland-history-of-chicago-v1.yaml is the pointer to it, which is why the two small OCR artifacts are deposited under chicago/reference/ — they are what makes this index re-derivable by someone who does not hold the scan.
